name: Kotor
title: Kotor Cruise Ship Thickness Gauging | UTM in the Bay
description: Ultrasonic thickness gauging at Kotor, Montenegro for cruise ships, expedition vessels and small passenger ships: scrubber piping, hull and tank boundaries.
h1: Ultrasonic Thickness Gauging for Ships Calling at Kotor
intro: Kotor lies at the head of the Bay of Kotor, beneath the walls of its old town, and is one of the best-known cruise calls on the Adriatic. Large cruise ships berth at the town quay or anchor in the inner bay, and smaller passenger ships and yachts use the same water. Gauging is mostly scrubber piping and technical spaces on a call day. Atlantis NDT brings thickness technicians from India for each ship, with no staff based in Montenegro.

highlights.h: Cruise calls under the old town walls
highlights.p: Several cruise ships can lie at the Kotor quay on a busy day while others anchor in the inner bay and tender passengers ashore, so gauging has to fit tight itineraries and the crowded water around them.

Cruise ships with exhaust gas cleaning systems carry wash-water and overboard piping that ages quickly. A call day is often long enough to gauge accessible runs, valves and the shell plating around the discharge.

highlights.h: A calm inner bay beyond Verige
highlights.p: Past the Verige narrows the water is sheltered from the open Adriatic, which suits owner's condition gauging of small passenger vessels, yachts and expedition ships on a lay-by berth or at anchor.

port.h: The port of Kotor and the inner Bay of Kotor
p: The Bay of Kotor is a drowned river valley, a sequence of basins linked by narrow channels and ringed by steep limestone mountains. Ships coming from the open sea enter past the Luštica peninsula, pass Herceg Novi and Tivat, and squeeze through the Verige strait before reaching the innermost basin, where Kotor sits. The passage is slow and demands attention from the pilot and bridge team, which is one reason ships stay for a full call rather than a brief stop. Winds are generally gentler inside the bay than outside, although squalls come down off the mountains.

Kotor's commercial identity today is passenger traffic. Cruise ships of many sizes arrive on most summer days, mooring at the town quay or anchoring in the inner bay and landing passengers by tender. Smaller cruise ships, expedition vessels and day-trip boats work the same waters, and a few cargo and service ships call at the port for local supply. The cruise calendar is concentrated between spring and autumn, with very little in winter, so any work that needs a ship out of passenger service falls in the off months.

For gauging, this places the emphasis on what can be done while a ship is working. The call day gives access to scrubber systems, ballast tank boundaries, technical spaces, sea water cooling lines and deck areas, and the long approach through the bay gives owners reason to confirm condition before a ship commits to the itinerary. Ships with a docking due usually leave Montenegro for a yard elsewhere in the Adriatic, so readings taken at Kotor serve as the pre-docking record that the yard and the attending surveyor will use.

facilities.h: Where gauging is practical at Kotor
p: The main working place is the cruise quay below the old town. Ships alongside can be gauged on the call day once the ship's safety officer and the chief engineer have agreed the spaces, with scrubber discharge lines and pump rooms a regular target. The quay is shared, so the berth allocation and the passenger programme set the time available, and the ship's agent confirms both before the team travels. Work in engine spaces is done under the ship's permit system, and results are reported against the spaces actually accessed.

At the inner-bay anchorage, a launch carries the team to the ship. This route suits smaller passenger vessels, yachts and expedition ships that stay several days, as well as ships between charters. There is no commercial drydock at Kotor itself. For ships needing steel renewal, the Bay's own shipyard at Bijela and yards on the Croatian and Italian coasts are the usual alternatives, and a pre-docking gauging record from Kotor helps that yard estimate steel before the ship is out of the water.
list: Kotor town quay: scrubber discharge piping, sea water lines and technical spaces on cruise ships during the call day
Inner-bay anchorage: launch-borne gauging of small passenger ships, expedition vessels and yachts in sheltered water
Lay-by berths for small passenger craft: tank boundary and deck gauging during lay-up or between charters
Cargo and supply berth: hatch covers and deck piping on service ships calling for local supply
Pre-docking gauging for ships bound for Bijela or Adriatic yards: a steel estimate before the ship leaves the bay

context.h: Port state control, class rules and the Montenegrin setting
p: Montenegro is a member of the Paris MoU, so foreign ships calling at Kotor are exposed to the same targeting and inspection regime as at ports in neighbouring Croatia and Italy. Passenger ships get close attention in any regime, and an inspector will look at structural condition, fire safety and the integrity of scrubber and ballast arrangements. A thickness record taken before the call gives the superintendent a view of known weak areas, so that nothing surprising is found by someone else first.

Montenegro is a candidate for EU membership but is not in the EU, and the Montenegrin Maritime Safety Administration is the national authority for ships and ports. Voyages that start or end in an EU port still come under EU ETS and FuelEU Maritime, which affects cruise operators running itineraries between Croatia, Italy, Greece and Kotor. Cruise owners therefore watch hull and machinery condition closely when planning refits, and gauging data is one of the inputs. Visiting technicians also follow Montenegrin entry rules, which differ from the Schengen system.

jobs.h: Typical thickness gauging jobs at Kotor
jobs.p: Kotor jobs are short, planned around an itinerary and often repeated across a season. A cruise ship may allow a few hours at the quay; a small passenger vessel or yacht at the inner anchorage may allow days. We confirm berth, access to spaces and reporting format with the superintendent in advance, and build visa lead time for Montenegro into the schedule from the day the enquiry arrives.
list: Scrubber overboard piping and discharge valve gauging on a cruise ship at the Kotor quay, completed during the passenger programme ashore
Sea chest and sea water cooling line readings on a mid-size cruise ship ahead of its winter shipyard period
Ballast tank boundary gauging on an expedition ship at the inner anchorage between voyages
Hull plating and tank readings on a small passenger vessel at a lay-by berth, giving a pre-purchase view for a prospective buyer
Pre-docking steel estimate on a coastal passenger ship before it sails for a yard in the Adriatic

logistics: Tivat Airport, on the same bay, is the closest, with seasonal European links, and Dubrovnik Airport in Croatia is reachable by road across the border. Podgorica Airport has year-round connections and a longer road transfer to the coast. The ship's agent arranges quay passes and launches at Kotor. Montenegro sets its own entry rules for visitors, so we check what Indian passport holders need on the date of the enquiry rather than relying on general assumptions.
vessels: Small cruise ships and expedition vessels

faqs.q: How long does a cruise ship stay at Kotor, and is that enough for gauging?
faqs.a: Most cruise ships stay for a day, and the working window is shorter than the call. That is enough for scrubber piping, selected sea water lines and a few technical spaces if access is agreed beforehand. Larger scopes, such as tank boundaries, are better scheduled during lay-up or a shipyard period.

faqs.q: Is there a drydock at Kotor?
faqs.a: No. The shipyard at Bijela, elsewhere in the Bay of Kotor, and yards on the Croatian and Italian coasts are the usual choices. Gauging at Kotor before the ship leaves gives the yard steel estimates for its specification, and the technicians can travel on to the yard for the docking survey so measurement points stay consistent.

faqs.q: Can you gauge a ship at the inner-bay anchorage?
faqs.a: Yes, by launch arranged through the agent. It works well for small passenger ships, expedition vessels and yachts that stay for several days. We confirm sea conditions with the master and the agent on the day, since squalls descending from the mountains can briefly suspend launch operations.

faqs.q: Does Montenegro's status outside the EU change how you plan a Kotor job?
faqs.a: It mainly affects entry rules for our Indian technicians, which are Montenegrin and not Schengen. We check the requirements when the enquiry arrives and include the lead time. Port state control follows Paris MoU practice, so the inspection regime is the one superintendents already know from neighbouring ports.
